It marked the ninth time in Cain's career -- including starts of varying lengths -- that he had yielded just one hit. Cain pitched one of his best games against Washington last July 24, when he spun a four-hit shutout in a 1-0 Giants triumph. He's 3-2 with a 2.36 ERA in six lifetime outings against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann started the game on Thursday for Washington and had serious problems in the first inning against the Dodgers. After striking out leadoff hitter Rafael Furcal, Zimmermann couldn't get the next six hitters out. The first run scored on an RBI single by James Loney. Four batters later, Matt Kemp hit a grand slam over the right-center-field wall. Casey Blake followed and hit what looked like a routine fly ball to right-center field, but center fielder Elijah Dukes and right fielder Adam Dunn did not communicate on who was catching the ball, which dropped in for a triple. Dunn said that a fan in the stands called for the ball, and Dunn and Dukes thought the other called for the ball. Blake then scored on a sacrifice fly by Dodgers starter Randy Wolf. After that, Zimmermann retired the next nine hitters he faced. He went on to pitch six innings and give up six runs.

home_pitcher_note: Not long ago, a strong outing from Zito would be regarded as an aberration. Now it's considered almost routine. Zito's resurgence bodes well for him and the Giants, since he's typically a second-half pitcher. Entering this year he was 53-57 with a 4.14 ERA lifetime before the All-Star break and 70-36, 3.47 afterward.
away_pitcher_note: Six days after pitching the first complete game of his career, Martis lasted only 5 1/3 innings on Friday, but it was good enough to help the Nationals defeat the Diamondbacks, 5-4, at Chase Field. Martis allowed three of the four runs on nine hits, while striking out six batters and walking two. What made this start impressive was that Martis was able to get out of jams. For example, after Chris Young tripled home Felipe Lopez to cut the lead to 4-2 with no outs in the fifth inning, Young was left stranded at third. Martis struck out Justin Upton and Mark Reynolds and got Josh Whitesell to fly out to right fielder Austin Kearns. The entire season has been good for Martis, 22. He now leads the Nationals with four wins, which ranks second in the National League.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez has made one quality start in five tries, so he needs some instant results. He recorded a 9.00 ERA in his last two starts and worked only nine innings in that span. Sanchez has made four appearances against the Mets in his caareer, posting a 2-1 mark with a 3.55 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Despite what he called an awful bullpen session, which translated into awful stuff during the game, Maine managed to hold the Pirates to one run in six innings last Saturday. summary: 2009-05-14 - New York Mets (7) @ San Francisco Giants (4) (Final)

summary: 2009-05-15 - New York Mets (8) @ San Francisco Giants (6) (Final)

Now he faces the Giants against whom he pitched five scoreless innings in one appearance last season. He won that game, his lone decision in three career starts against San Francisco. summary: 2009-05-16 - New York Mets (9) @ San Francisco Giants (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Cain gave up four earned runs in seven innings Tuesday against the Nationals, three of the runs on a three-run blast by Nick Johnson. Cain is 2-3 in his career against the Mets with a 5.23 ERA in five starts. Last year he gave up five runs in five innings in his only start against them.
away_pitcher_note: From 7.20 to 8.10 to 6.32 to 6.00 to 5.46 to 4.89. Pelfrey's ERA is shrinking now. He no longer winces at the sight of it. Now he opposes team he has faced once previously. He pitched seven scoreless innings against them in a game he won last July. Current members of the Giants roster have merely 27 at-bats and five hits against him combined.
summary: 2009-05-17 - New York Mets (0) @ San Francisco Giants (2) (Final)

He allowed back-to-back homers -- by Alfonso Soriano and Theriot -- to start the bottom of the first and needed 39 pitches to finish the inning. He is 2-4 in 10 career starts with a 3.10 ERA against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Zito made his fifth strong outing in a row last Wednesday, but luck conspired against him in a 6-3 Giants loss to Washington. Zito blanked the Nationals for four innings and entered the seventh trailing just 1-0. But Elijah Dukes' two-run, two-out, broken-bat bloop single off reliever Merkin Valdez resulted in Zito being charged with four runs in 6 1/3 innings. summary: 2009-05-19 - San Francisco Giants (1) @ San Diego Padres (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Gaudin struggled with his command in his last outing. Gaudin needed 102 pitches to get 13 outs. Gaudin blamed the walks and a high pitch count for his struggles in the start.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez had yet another uneven start last Thursday as he yielded four runs in 5 2/3 innings against the New York Mets. He will see San Diego's lineup for the second time this season, though he'll be aiming for better results this time around. summary: 2009-05-20 - San Francisco Giants (1) @ San Diego Padres (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: If nothing else, Correia stands as an answer to a unique trivia question: The Padres went from April 16 to May 15 without a victory from a starting pitcher. away_pitcher_note: There's a reason the guy they call "Timmy" is atop the Giants rotation. In his third season at the big league level, he stands 19 strikeouts shy of 500. Despite leaving with a six-inning lead Friday against the New York Mets, however, the reigning National League Cy Young Award winner was charged with five earned runs and is winless in his last two starts. summary: 2009-05-21 - San Francisco Giants (2) @ San Diego Padres (3) (Final)

It was his second straight start in which he lasted at least five innings but he'll need to work deeper into the game -- he threw 98 pitches. He is penciled in against San Francisco.
away_pitcher_note: The Big Unit will return to the city where he became truly big, as an All-Star and Cy Young Award winner between 1989-98. But the 45-year-old has struggled recently, recording an 11.05 ERA in his last three starts. That's based on 18 earned runs allowed in 14 2/3 innings, to go with three walks and 12 strikeouts. Johnson has pitched progressively fewer innings in that span, lasting 5 2/3 May 6 at Colorado, five on May 11 against Washington and four-plus last Saturday against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: For the second time this season, Olson has been tabbed as an emergency starter, getting Saturday night's assignment in place of lefty Jarrod Washburn. Olson, acquired from the Cubs in late January, went five innings against the Red Sox on May 16 and surrendered five runs in taking the loss. Three of the five hits he gave up to the Red Sox were home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Despite walking five batters, Cain tossed six scoreless innings in his last start, Sunday against the Mets. home_pitcher_note: The best start of Hernandez's career has been knocked back a few notches during a winless month of May. It was a total reversal from his previous start, when he held the Rangers scoreless over seven innings. Hernandez has faced the Giants once in his MLB career and notched one of his four Interleague wins.
away_pitcher_note: Zito has reclaimed his 2002 American League Cy Young form. He also has stolen Matt Cain's dubious distinction as the Giants' hard-luck pitcher, having received 1.81 runs per game -- the worst support among NL pitchers. Zito has surged in his last six starts, posting a 2.21 ERA in that span. He has allowed only four home runs this season, though two came in his last outing at San Diego -- a complete-game effort in a 2-1 loss.

It was Sanchez's third consecutive losing decision but also just his second quality start of the year. Sanchez has struggled against Atlanta, going 0-2 with a 7.04 ERA in three appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez finally recorded his first win at Turner Field this season in an abbreviated outing during the Braves' 12-3 win over the Rockies on Wednesday. The Braves' offensive outburst gave Vazquez's arm a welcome reprieve. He threw just 71 pitches on Wednesday after averaging 111 pitches per game over his previous three starts. Vazquez has been stingy with runs of late. Including his five innings with no earned runs against the Rockies, Vazquez has given up two earned runs or fewer in each of his last three starts.

Lincecum has thrived in his limited number of appearances against Atlanta, going 4-0 with a 2.70 ERA in four career appearances, including 2-0, 1.72 last year.
away_pitcher_note: Medlen looks to shake off a disastrous Major League debut against the Rockies on Thursday. In that outing, Medlen pitched just three-plus innings, allowing five earned runs on three hits, five walks, a hit batter, a balk and two wild pitches. Medlen posted superb numbers in Triple-A Gwinnett before getting called up to Atlanta. For Gwinnett, he was a perfect 5-0 with a 1.19 ERA. This will be the first road start of his career.

home_pitcher_note: Rebounding from a three start stretch in which he was 1-2 with an 11.05 ERA and a .403 opponents' batting average, Johnson yielded one run and six hits in 5 1/3 innings last Friday at Seattle. This will be the 45-year-old's third attempt at career victory No. 299. Johnson has been relatively so-so against Atlanta, posting a 5-5 record with a 4.33 ERA in 12 career appearances against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: On Friday night against the Blue Jays, Kawakami provided the kind of outing that the Braves had in mind when they signed him. Perhaps most importantly, Kawakami completed a start without walking a batter for this first time this season. The Japanese import seemed to get stronger as the game went on, maintaining his low-90s fastball into the eighth inning. This will be Kawakami's first start against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Buckner was pushed back a few days due to Thursday's off day, and the D-backs desire to keep Dan Haren and Jon Garland as close to regular rest as possible. That was similar to his first start, when he allowed just one run over 7 1/3 innings against the A's in Oakland. In both of those games, Buckner was aggressive in the strike zone and mixed his pitches well. In the middle start, when he allowed five runs in five innings against the Padres, Buckner nibbled at the zone a little too much. He does not possess a dominating fastball so he must hit his spots with it and use his out pitch -- a 12-to-6 curve -- effectively.
away_pitcher_note: Cain has mostly avoided the lousy luck -- poor run support or leaky relief pitching -- that plagued him in previous seasons. One exception occurred on April 26 of this season, when he pitched well enough to win at Arizona. He yielded one run -- a Mark Reynolds homer -- and four hits in seven innings, but the Giants ultimately lost, 5-4, in 12 innings. Cain is 3-3 with a 3.18 ERA in 11 career starts against Arizona. Much of his success has been due to his toughness with men on base. The right-hander has limited opponents to a .111 batting average with runners in scoring position, the best in the Majors through last weekend.

home_pitcher_note: Davis finally got back into the win column last Friday in San Diego. The left-hander tossed six shutout innings in an 8-0 Arizona win. It was his first victory since April 29 a span of six starts. Davis allowed three hits and walked four while striking out five. He pitched well enough to win in his start before that, but instead came away with a no decision against the Braves at Chase Field. The left-hander allowed two runs on seven hits over seven innings. Both of the runs came in the third inning and Davis was lights out after that. The D-backs managed to rally and tie the game before winning in 11 innings. This is the final year of a three-year extension he signed after coming over the Arizona from Milwaukee prior to the 2007 season.
away_pitcher_note: Zito ended a personal four-game losing streak in his most recent start despite showing less than his best. Last Friday at Florida, he threw just 59 strikes out of his 95 pitches and was removed after walking the first two batters in the sixth inning. Yet he allowed only one run in five innings and earned the win in San Francisco's 2-1 triumph. Zito has consistently downplayed his own record while prioritizing the team's fortunes, but as he said afterward, victories are "the last thing we control, but it's the first thing people mention."

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer did not pitch poorly in his last start, but he did not pitch great, either. The right-hander tossed five shutout innings against the Padres at PETCO Park, but ran up his pitch count in the process because once again he struggled to hit his spots. Scherzer walked five and allowed three hits in the five innings. In fairness, Scherzer did leave with a 2-0 lead and could have easily picked up the win. The Arizona bullpen, though, gave up a six-spot in the sixth and the D-backs wound up losing 6-4. In his outing prior to that, Scherzer had the worst game of his Major League career against the Braves. He missed with his location, particularly against left-handed hitters, and Atlanta punished him for it. Scherzer gave up a career-high eight runs on 10 hits while lasting just 3 2/3 innings. Three batters into the game, the Braves led 2-0 and a two-run homer by Chipper Jones in the third added to the woes. Garret Anderson's three-run shot in the fourth capped Scherzer's day.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez didn't exactly get off to a rousing start in his efforts to duplicate the excellence he sustained last June, which he completed with a 5-1 record and a 3.10 ERA in six games. In his last start, Sanchez lasted only 4 2/3 innings while allowing eight hits and all of the Marlins' runs in a 5-4 Giants defeat last Saturday. It wasn't a completely dismal performance by Sanchez, who threw 67 strikes in 101 pitches and struck out seven, matching a season high. Sanchez must continue that trend to build his durability, which has been lacking this season. He has pitched past the sixth inning just once, largely explaining why he has recorded just two quality starts out of 10.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum has won five consecutive decisions over a span of nine starts. away_pitcher_note: With an impressive outing of five-hit, shutout ball in his home debut -- a 3-0 win against the Orioles -- Mazzaro extended his career-opening scoreless streak to 13 2/3 innings, which passed Aaron Harang (11 scoreless innings) for the longest such streak for a starter in A's history. After his shaky frame, Outman settled down to retire the next seven batters to set the team up for a win. This will mark the rookie's first career start against San Francisco.

away_pitcher_note: Coming off his best start thus far in the big leagues -- a seven-inning shutout performance in Chicago -- Anderson was rocked for 10 hits and five runs courtesy an offensive explosion from a pent-up Twins lineup en route to a 10-5 A's loss on Tuesday. Following a one-run showing through five innings, Anderson found himself struggling with command in the sixth and let the ball get up in the zone one too many times. This will mark the 21-year-old rookie's first career start against the Giants.

away_pitcher_note: Holland is 0-3 with a 7.08 ERA in four starts and has an 8.54 ERA in his last seven games to raise his ERA from 1.74. home_pitcher_note: Cahill, the A's rookie right-hander, won Wednesday against the Los Angeles Dodgers despite not having his best stuff on the mound. Cahill walked three batters to load the bases in the first before escaping the jam. Then in the second, he saw Matt Kemp reach third with one out but Cahill again didn't yield a run. Cahill did allow a run in the fifth and sixth innings, but those two runs were unearned. In all, Cahill pitched 5 1/3 innings and allowed two runs (zero earned) on four hits. The win was Cahill's fourth of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Thanks to another uneven start, Sanchez's ERA sailed north of five for the third time this season. Tuesday against the Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim, the lefty yielded seven runs (six earned) over 3 2/3 innings. Sanchez is winless in his last four starts and has a strikeout-to-walk ratio of 17-to-12 during that span. He won his lone start against the Oakland Athletics last season, allowing just one earned run in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Mazzaro pitched well Thursday night at Dodger Stadium in his fourth career start. He worked quickly and did not hesitate to challenge the Dodgers hitters. Mazzaro managed to escape trouble in the bottom of the second when Orlando Cabrera stole a couple of RBIs from Russell Martin with a leaping grab at short. Mazzaro gave up a home run in the third to Orlando Hudson and allowed another run in the fifth, but he pitched well enough to win. In all, Mazzaro lasted six innings and gave up two runs on five hits. Mazzaro is 0-1 in his career against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum was at or near his best through seven innings against the Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim on Wednesday. In the eighth, however, he yielded three runs and ended up with his first loss since April 12. The right-hander struck out nine Angels and has whiffed at least seven in 11 of his 14 starts this season. During his campaign for the National League Cy Young Award last season, he threw seven shutout innings and got the win in his only start against the Oakland Athletics.

home_pitcher_note: With Josh Outman not expected to make the start because of tightness in his left forearm, all signs point to the return of the left-handed Gonzalez, who is 4-1 with a 2.51 ERA in 12 starts at Sacramento this season. Gio Gonzalez, whose 71 strikeouts in 61 innings rank second in the Pacific Coast League, has been recalled to Oakland twice this season, and twice he was sent down the day after pitching in long relief. In those two games, he gave up seven earned runs on 11 hits and seven walks while striking out 11, but his command in Sacramento had been improving all year -- his strikeouts-to-walks ratio is now better than 2-to-1.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson's ERA crept back up to five after allowing four runs in 5 2/3 innings of work against the Texas Rangers Friday, taking a no-decision. The lefty had won three of his previous four starts. Johnson allowed two earned runs on three hits over seven innings in his last start against the Oakland Athletics on June 13. He's 14-9 all-time when facing the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo pitched seven solid innings against the Tigers on Sunday, but was burned by one bad pitch, a hanging slider to Brandon Inge that Inge deposited in the left-field seats for a decisive, three-run home run. The Tigers managed just six other hits -- all singles -- off Gallardo in his best start since he worked eight shutout innings in Atlanta on June 5. He hit a three-run home run of his own to beat Randy Johnson and the Giants on April 8 at AT&T Park and will be facing San Francisco for the fourth time in his career. He made his Major League debut against them on June 18, 2007, pitching 6 1/3 innings for a win.
away_pitcher_note: Cain allowed just one run over eight innings against the Texas Rangers Saturday but came up empty in the 'W' column. He has 17 strikeouts in his last two outings, compared with just three walks. Cain last pitched against the Milwaukee Brewers on April 9, when he allowed one run in seven innings and picked up the win.

home_pitcher_note: McClung will step into the rotation to replace left-hander Manny Parra, who was demoted on June 13 ahead of a stretch in which the Brewers needed just four starters. Manager Ken Macha was hesitant to remove McClung from the bullpen because he was such a key cog there over the first three months of the season (3.24 ERA 28 games, .242 opponents' average) but necessity won out. McClung filled both roles for the Brewers in 2008, when he went 4-4 with a 4.24 ERA in 12 starts and 2-2 with a 3.67 ERA in 25 relief appearances. He made his 2009 season debut on Opening Day in San Francisco, issuing three walks in two innings but limiting the damage to one hit and one run.
away_pitcher_note: Zito looked like his younger self Sunday when he carried a no-hit bid into the seventh inning against the Texas Rangers. He finished the game having allowed two runs on two hits over seven solid innings. The lefty struck out a season-high eight batters. Despite his win Sunday, run support remains an issue: Zito has received three runs or less from his teammates in 13 of his 14 starts this season. He lost his lone start against the Milwaukee Brewers last season, allowing three runs on eight hits over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan was a victim of some bad defensive plays in his last outing against Minnesota. Suppan gave up nine hits in five innings, giving up seven runs, four of which were earned. Three of the other four runs also could have been avoided, when a swinging strike three got past catcher Jason Kendall to load the bases in the top of the first. The next batter followed with a bases-clearing double to put the Brewers in a hole they wouldn't get out of. Suppan and the Brewers opened the season against the Giants on April 7, with Suppan taking the loss in a 10-6 loss for the Brewers, allowing six runs in four innings. For his career Suppan has had mixed results against the Giants, going 3-5 with a 5.64 ERA in nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Sadowski last pitched June 20 against Colorado Springs, receiving no decision as he allowed 10 hits and four earned runs in six innings. His most impressive recent effort came against Portland on May 30, when he yielded three hits in six shutout innings. Sadowski limited right-handed batters to a .209 average in Triple-A, compared with .281 against left-handers. San Francisco obtained Sadowski by selecting him in the 12th round of the 2003 First-Year Player Draft.

home_pitcher_note: Thompson was better than his line might have indicated his last time out, but this still might be his last start for a while. Kyle Lohse is due back from the disabled list in short order, so Thompson needs to state his case to stay in the rotation, and he needs to do it soon. He's filled a lot of roles, from long man to late-inning reliever to starter, but it's pitching in the rotation that he enjoys most. If he wants to keep doing it, he'd be well advised to turn in a strong showing on Monday.
away_pitcher_note: If not for Jason Giambi's solo home run, Tim Lincecum would have tallied his second shutout of the season Tuesday against the Oakland Athletics. That doesn't mean he had an easy go of it, though. Twice Lincecum evaded bases-loaded situations by inducing groundball double plays. He's won three of his last four starts. The right-hander went 2-0 with a 1.38 ERA against the St. Louis Cardinals last season.
summary: 2009-06-29 - San Francisco Giants (10) @ St. Louis Cardinals (0) (Final)

With only one more start before All-Stars are chosen, the loss may have cost him a chance to pitch in the Midsummer Classic, but few in the National League have been better this year. Carpenter is throwing everything he's got and throwing it all for quality strikes -- fastball, cutter, curveball and changeup. He's a handful, though once again it appears that he'll be facing off against a fellow former Cy Young Award winner -- for fourth time this year.
away_pitcher_note: Randy Johnson pitched seven strong innings for the fourth time this season Wednesday against the Oakland Athletics. Johnson allowed one run on six hits and struck out six. He's now won three starts in a row and five of his last six. In two games against the St. Louis Cardinals last season, the Big Unit went 0-1 with an ERA of 9.31.
summary: 2009-06-30 - San Francisco Giants (6) @ St. Louis Cardinals (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright has settled into something of a pattern this year. He hasn't been efficient, getting into trouble far too often and running up high pitch counts. But he's shown an ability to limit the damage, locking down with men on base. It's added up to a lot of good-but-not-great starts. The problem is that Wainwright and the team expect closer to great from Wainwright, who was the Opening Day starter at Busch Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Cain allowed all five runs, matching his season-worst, in last Friday's 5-1 loss at Milwaukee. But he still managed to look mostly effective, allowing six hits in seven innings and striking out nine. The decision ended his personal seven-game winning streak over a span of nine starts. Cain, who appears bound for the National League All-Star squad, has worked at least six innings in every start and has recorded 10 quality starts in 15 outings. He's living up to his workhorse reputation by averaging 105 pitches per game.
summary: 2009-07-01 - San Francisco Giants (1) @ St. Louis Cardinals (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Manager Tony La Russa declined to comment on Wellemeyer's status in the rotation after another rough start on Saturday, but it's clear the right-hander needs to turn it around. For now, the Cardinals don't feel like they have any other really viable options, so the chances are very good that Wellemeyer will make this start. However, also on Thursday, Kyle Lohse will make a Minor League rehabilitation start as he tries to recover from a right forearm injury. It may not be a coincidence that the two starts occur on the same day.
away_pitcher_note: Despite his record and ERA, Zito has improved visibly this season. He's averaging four walks per nine innings, down from 5.1 last year, and he leads the staff with 11 double-play grounders induced. Zito's coming off an encouraging start in which he shut out Milwaukee for five innings at Miller Park, where he had lost his previous three outings and recorded a 10.05 ERA. Zito's night ended when Prince Fielder belted a three-run homer in the sixth inning. But it still represented a significant improvement for Zito, who lost to St. Louis on May 30 when he allowed three runs and 10 hits in 6 2/3 innings.
summary: 2009-07-02 - San Francisco Giants (2) @ St. Louis Cardinals (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Sadowski was a sensation in his Major League debut last Sunday at Milwaukee, allowing four hits in six shutout innings as the Giants prevailed, 7-0. Sadowski, who struck out only two batters, can reach the low-90 mph range with his fastball but relies mostly on location and late movement. He displayed adequate control against the Brewers, issuing three walks. Sadowski became the first Giants pitcher to win his Major League debut since Joe Nathan in 1999.
away_pitcher_note: Paulino turned in his best performance of the season last time out against the Tigers. Making his first since June 7 after being on the disabled list with a strained right groin, the right-hander set career highs in strike outs and innings pitched, fanning nine over seven frames of three-hit ball. Paulino allowed just one run and retired the last 10 batters he faced, earning his first win as a starter this season. Paulino has never faced the Giants in his career. He is 0-1 with an 8.01 ERA in two starts against the National League West this season, both coming against the Colorado Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum outdid himself last Monday at St. Louis, firing a two-hit shutout. It was the third shutout of his career and second of the season. Lincecum remains overpowering -- he struck out 12 two starts ago at Oakland -- but he has relied more and more on "pitching to contact" and putting batters away earlier in the count, thus reducing wear and tear on his valuable arm. Nevertheless, Lincecum's 21-4 with a 2.06 ERA when he strikes out at least eight batters in a game. He's 1-0 with a 2.13 ERA in four career starts against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Ortiz solidified his spot in the starting rotation by holding Detroit to six hits and two runs while striking out five batters in 7 1/3 innings on Sunday. He would have won the game had closer Jose Valverde not blown the save in the ninth inning. Ortiz enjoyed some of his best years in San Francisco, going 69-47 in six seasons with the Giants, including an 18-9 record in 1999. Against the Giants, he's 0-3 with a 7.46 ERA in seven starts. Ortiz is 20-15 with a 3.64 ERA in 56 career games at AT&T Park, including 53 starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Big Unit picked up career victory No. 303 last Tuesday at St. Louis. Two Albert Pujols home runs marred his 5 1/3-inning performance, but Johnson yielded just two other hits as the Giants prevailed, 6-3. If Johnson's pitching, expect reliever Brian Wilson to follow at some point. Wilson has saved each of Johnson's victories, marking the eighth time in big league history that one pitcher saved a teammate's first eight wins in a season. Johnson, who was 10-1 for the Astros in the second half of the 1998 season, is 4-1 in seven career starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: After winning one game in the first two months of the regular season, Oswalt went 3-2 with a 3.14 ERA in six starts in June. He's coming off his best start of the season, a two-hitter at San Diego on Monday, in which the only run scored on a wild pitch. He's 4-5 with a 3.98 ERA in 12 career starts against the Giants, and 2-5 with a 4.96 ERA in eight career starts at AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: Cain is winless in his last three starts, though he has pitched more than capably over that stretch. He received no decision while allowing one run and three hits in eight innings against Texas on June 20, lost at Milwaukee on June 26 while yielding five runs in seven innings and took another no-decision at St. Louis in his last start despite surrendering just one run in seven innings. In Cain's 16 starts, he has been unable to last at least six innings only once, and that was a rain-shortened complete game at Washington on June 4.
away_pitcher_note: West took a no-decision in his last start despite not having his best stuff as the Nationals tagged him for five runs on eight hits over 4 1/3 innings. The tall left-hander struggled from the start and had trouble with Washington's best hitters as Adam Dunn and Ryan Zimmerman combined to go 4-for-6 with two doubles, a home run and three RBIs. West will try to repeat his success against the Giants in his next start. The 23-year-old picked up his first Major League win against San Francisco when he threw eight shutout innings of two-hit ball on June 8.

home_pitcher_note: Facing Florida has been a happy activity for Zito, who's 3-0 in four career starts against the Marlins. Typically a stronger performer in the season's second half (70-36, 3.47 entering this year, compared to 53-57, 4.14 in the first half), Zito probably wouldn't mind kicking himself into gear a start early. He has worked past the sixth inning in only one of his last six outings. The Giants are 3-3 in those games and 7-9 overall when Zito starts.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson had his shortest outing of the season, allowing one run on five hits over 3 1/3 innings, in which he struck out three and walked four. The Marlins ace struggled from the start and did not appear to have his best command as he fell behind hitters throughout the outing. The big right-hander will look to rebound from his disappointing start against the Nationals when he takes the ball in San Francisco to face the Giants. Johnson has held the current crop of Giants to a .243 career average against him and has allowed just one extra base hit, a double by Randy Winn.

home_pitcher_note: Two starts into his Major League career, Ryan Sadowski has nailed down the No. 5 spot in the Giants starting rotation. All has gone his way thus far. The Giants lineup has supported him with 20 runs of support and the right-hander has been pitching to contact, employing his two-seam, sinking fastball. He's retired just six batters on strikes in his 13 innings, but has also yielded just seven hits.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad continues to get hurt by the home run ball. The 22-year-old gave up two homers over the first two innings in his last start against the Pirates. The right-hander allowed four runs in three innings before being lifted after a 45-minute rain delay. Volstad has allowed 15 home runs on the season and at least one in eight of his last ten starts.

home_pitcher_note: Tim Lincecum hasn't allowed a run in 23 innings. Heck, he hasn't even allowed a runner past second base in 18 frames. The NL Pitcher of the Month for June got off to a great start in July, tossing seven shutout innings against the Houston Astros on Saturday. He struck out nine batters and allowed just three hits. Lincecum is 0-1 in two starts against the San Diego Padres this season.
away_pitcher_note: Geer tossed 6 1/3 innings while allowing two runs on seven hits in his last start, a 7-4 Padres win against the Dodgers at PETCO Park. Geer walked none and struck out one in his fourth consecutive quality start. He allowed one home run -- a solo shot by Manny Ramirez in the first inning. Geer said the pitch was a hanging changeup that Ramirez took advantage of to launch his first home run since returning from a 50-game suspension.
summary: 2009-07-09 - San Diego Padres (3) @ San Francisco Giants (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Randy Johnson will not take his regular turn in the Giants rotation after he was placed on the 15-day disabled list Monday with a strained left shoulder. In the Big Unit's stead, Sanchez will make his first start since he was relegated to the bullpen on June 27. Sanchez tossed three shutout innings in that role, last pitching on July 3. In two starts against the San Diego Padres this season, Sanchez is 0-2, having allowed seven earned runs in 10 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Banks struggled in his first start this season after two pretty good long-relief outings. Facing the Dodgers on July 5, the right-hander allowed home runs to Casey Blake, Andre Ethier and even pitcher Chad Billingsley. All told, Banks, who didn't factor in the decision after the Padres came back with five runs in the ninth inning to force extra innings, allowed six runs in 4 1/3 innings.  Banks will return to AT&T Park, where he had the best outing of his career a year ago when he allowed one run in a complete-game victory over the Giants.
summary: 2009-07-10 - San Diego Padres (0) @ San Francisco Giants (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Cain has been dominant this season, allowing one earned run or less over at least six innings in 10 starts. Lifetime, Cain is 39-15 when he receives two or more runs of support. That improves to 35-6 when San Francisco scores at least three runs for him, including 9-0 this year. He has made 12 quality starts in 17 outings, and, not coincidentally, the Giants are 12-5 in his appearances. Cain's next assignment after this one will be his first career All-Star Game.
away_pitcher_note: Stauffer makes his first appearance in the Major Leagues since 2007 when he made two starts with the Padres. Stauffer, who had shoulder surgery a year ago, was 2-1 with a 2.14 ERA between Double-A San Antonio and Triple-A Portland. He was 2-1 with a 2.35 ERA in four starts with Portland and tossed eight scoreless innings in a victory over Colorado Springs last week. Stauffer is 4-7 with a 6.37 ERA in 18 career Major League games. He was 0-1 with a 21.13 ERA in two starts in 2007.
summary: 2009-07-11 - San Diego Padres (1) @ San Francisco Giants (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Zito's coming off perhaps his best outing as a Giant, an 8 1/3-inning effort against the Florida Marlins, who mustered four hits. Zito permitted only one runner to reach scoring position while just missing his first complete game since April 2003. Zito, who has received the lowest average run support in the Major Leagues, is 0-1 in two starts this year against San Diego despite yielding only two runs and 11 hits in 15 innings. Zito's performance at home (2-3, 3.27 ERA) is superior to his showing on the road (3-5, 5.66).
away_pitcher_note: Correia turned in a quality start in his last outing against the D-backs on July 7, but took the loss, as he had a throwing error during an inning that saw the Padres commit three errors. Still, Correia, who has been remarkably consistent the last six weeks, pitched well, allowing three earned runs in six innings with two walks and six strikeouts. Correia has had a quality start -- six or more innings, three or fewer runs -- in six of his last seven starts. This will be the second time he's faced his former team, the Giants. On May 21, Correia allowed one run in 6 1/3 innings, but received a no-decision.
summary: 2009-07-12 - San Diego Padres (10) @ San Francisco Giants (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Maholm rebounded from one of his worst starts of the season to have a stellar performance in what was his final start of the first half. He was poised to pitch well past the sixth until the Pirates had to pull him for a pinch hitter. Still, he allowed just two runs on six hits. Maholm hasn't been as consistent from start-to-start as he'd like, but when he's been on, he's been dominant. Of the 56 runs he has allowed this season, half of them have been confined to four starts. In his other 14 starts, Maholm has allowed a total of just 28.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum carried a no-hit bid into the seventh inning Thursday against the Padres. He allowed three runs on three hits (and four walks) in 6 2/3 frames, ending his scoreless streak at 29 innings. Lincecum is 4-0 over his past four starts and has whiffed eight or more batters in six straight starts. The Giants' ace lost in his only career appearance against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Morton blamed his struggles last time out on both poor pitch selection and poor location. He made it through the Astros' order once without being hurt, but he would eventually be chased after allowing 10 hits and five runs in only four innings. When he's on, Morton has movement to his pitches that is better than anyone on the staff. Still, there are some growing pains to be expected as Morton continues to try and harness some of that movement.
away_pitcher_note: Giants manager Bruce Bochy planned to shift his rotation after the All-Star break, and he's done just that. With Randy Johnson on the DL (strained throwing shoulder), Zito slides into the No. 2 role, in between All-Star hurlers Tim Lincecum and Matt Cain. Maybe that will force Zito to pick up his game. Sunday against the light-hitting San Diego Padres, the lefty allowed nine earned runs on 10 hits over 4 1/3 innings. He hasn't pitched past the sixth inning in six of his last eight starts. Zito lost his lone start against the Pirates in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Duke threw his sixth career complete game in his last outing, with eight strong innings against the Phillies on July 10 -- but he still lost, 3-2, a running theme in Duke's season. Duke has lost four of his last five starts, with the Pirates scoring just seven runs in those four losses. In his eight losses this season, the Pirates have managed just 10 runs -- only eight while he has been in the game. Duke is 0-5 in his last seven road starts. It was Duke's third complete game this year, making him the first Pirates lefty since Denny Neagle in 1995 to throw three complete games in a season.
away_pitcher_note: Cain will begin the season's second half pitching out of the third slot in the rotation. He will have eight days of rest after he was hit by a line drive in his right (throwing) elbow on July 11. That play resulted in his shortest career start (1 2/3 innings) and forced Cain to cede his spot on the active All-Star roster. Cain's elbow was still sore as he headed to St. Louis, but X-rays ruled out a fracture, and he's expected to regain full strength in his arm simply by resting it. The right-hander will take his 1.17 ERA for July into his start against the Pirates. He went 0-1 with a 6.23 ERA in outings against Pittsburgh last season.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson has been one of baseball's top rookies since making his debut in June. He has yet to lose a game and beat the Yankees and Red Sox in consecutive starts. The right-hander seems to be getting better with each start, but had a rough outing in his introduction to Coors Field against the Rockies on July 9. He surrendered six hits and four runs in five innings. Hanson has never faced the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Following his July 10 no-hitter against the San Diego Padres, Sanchez has, to say the least, earned another start and a chance to stick in the rotation. He'll pitch out of the fourth slot for the first time this season, as Randy Johnson (strained throwing shoulder) works his way off the 15-day disabled list. Sanchez's historic performance came after two short relief appearances and plenty of side sessions in the bullpen. He'll take all of that experience into his outing against the Braves. The left-hander beat Atlanta on May 25, allowing two runs over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe fell victim to one rough inning against the Mets, surrendering three runs in the fourth and earning a no-decision. Other than that inning, Lowe was strong and allowed just five total hits on the day. The Braves still need him to get further into games as he failed to pitch at least seven innings for the first time since June 7 against the Pirates. Lowe is 4-5 against the Giants in his career with a 3.21 ERA. In four outings against the Giants last season, his only decision was a July 4 loss.
away_pitcher_note: All indications are that Sadowski will make his fourth career Major League start in this slot of the Giants' rotation. Not needing a fifth starter to end the season's first half, San Francisco optioned the right-hander to the Minor Leagues on July 9. Trying to stay sharp and keep on turn during the All-Star break, he allowed one run on five hits over six innings for Class A San Jose on Monday. Sadowski opened his big league career with two wins and and 16 2/3 scoreless innings. He allowed three runs (two earned) against the Florida Marlins on July 8, picking up his first loss.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens was again brilliant on Friday night that saw his team honor 355-game winner Greg Maddux, but his dominance was hardly needed. His teammates backed him with 11 runs against the Mets, while Jurrjens cruised to a two-hit shutout through six innings of work. The Curacao native left the game after throwing just 85 pitches to allow members of the Braves bullpen to get some work in the blowout. Jurrjens has now won consecutive starts for the first time since his first two starts of the season. He is winless against the Giants in two career starts.
away_pitcher_note: After throwing 35 pitches over two innings in the All-Star Game, Lincecum came back to fire 119 pitches in seven innings three days later at Pittsburgh. He performed to his usual standard, allowing one run and walking one while striking out 10 -- his 16th career double-digit strikeout game. Lincecum excels against most clubs, but he has been especially effective against the Braves, whom he has beaten five times in five career starts while posting a 2.08 ERA. That includes a May 26 game this season at AT&T Park, where Lincecum limited Atlanta to five hits over eight innings in a 4-0 San Francisco victory.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Kawakami gave the Braves his second successive quality start but took the loss as his offense couldn't mount anything against Mets starter Johan Santana. Kawakami matched the Mets' ace for five innings before losing command of the strike zone in the sixth. He walked in the game's first run and allowed another on a fielder's-choice groundout. Of his 100 pitches, only 56 were strikes. The Giants beat Kawakami on May 27, when the Japanese righty surrendered three earned runs in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Inconsistent all season, Zito took a two-hitter into the seventh inning on Saturday at Pittsburgh and trailed only 1-0, but he yielded a seventh-inning run as the Giants fell, 2-0. That thrust another hard-luck defeat upon Zito, who has received the poorest run support in the Major Leagues this season (32 runs in 19 games). The 2002 American League Cy Young Award winner has recorded nine quality starts and has coaxed a staff-high 12 double-play grounders. Zito has performed capably against Atlanta, going 2-1 with a 2.84 ERA in three career confrontations with the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Saturday at San Diego, Hammel struck out seven in 5 1/3 innings and gave up one run. He didn't figure in the decision, a 3-1 Rockies loss. The most memorable part of that game, however, was Hammel hitting the Padres' Edgar Gonzalez in the head with a 93-mph fastball. The pitch was clearly an accident, and Hammel said being able to talk to Gonzalez on the phone after the incident has eased his mind. Hammel threw six scoreless innings in his only start against the Giants this season, but San Francisco won, 1-0, in 10 innings on May 3.
away_pitcher_note: Cain won his second successive decision in his most recent start against the Pirates. The right-hander tossed seven dominating innings, giving up just one run on five hits. Cain also struck out eight batters, his highest total since June 26. He has faced the Rockies twice this season, coming in back-to-back starts on May 2 and 7. His second start was the better of the two, as he threw six shutout innings while surrendering just one hit.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa bordered on dominant while holding the D-backs to one run and four hits in seven innings of a victory at Coors Field on Monday night. Using a new sinker taught to him by staff ace Aaron Cook, De La Rosa is pitching more efficiently than at any point in his career. With the Rockies having changed their rotation to keep Jason Marquis on normal rest, De La Rosa will be pitching on five days' rest.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez followed up his July 10 no-hitter against San Diego in respectable fashion. Inconsistent through most of the season, Sanchez allowed three runs and just four hits in six innings at Atlanta last Monday. He wasn't involved in the decision as the Braves scored eight late runs to prevail, 11-3. Despite lacking command of his offspeed pitches, Sanchez struck out eight Braves and walked one, reflecting the wicked stuff he typically takes to the mound under any circumstances.

home_pitcher_note: Cook pitched through traffic, giving up eight hits in 6 1/3 innings. He gave up four runs, the last of which came after he was relieved for matchup purposes. Overall, though, it was a strong outing. Two of the runs came when center fielder Dexter Fowler misplayed a Justin Upton line drive into a triple.
away_pitcher_note: Sadowski might need a strong effort to save his spot in the rotation. After impressing the Giants with six- and seven-inning shutout efforts in his first two starts, he pitched respectably in a July 8 loss to Florida (two earned runs and five hits allowed in five innings), but the 26-year-old rookie was hit hard by the Atlanta Braves last Tuesday as he yielded eight runs and eight hits in 3 2/3 innings. After walking four batters in 13 innings spanning his first two starts, Sadowski has issued seven free passes -- one intentionally -- over 8 2/3 innings in his last two outings.

home_pitcher_note: The reigning National League Cy Young Award winner and two-time All-Star is 0-1 in his first two second-half starts despite pitching capably. Lincecum received no decision in the first game following the All-Star break, allowing one run and five hits while striking out 10 in seven innings at Pittsburgh on July 17. He followed that with a five-inning effort -- his shortest of the year since a three-inning cameo on Opening Day -- last Wednesday at Atlanta. Lincecum yielded four runs in that one, but struck out nine, proving that his arm and stuff remained sound.
away_pitcher_note: It was not a pretty sight the last time Maholm took the mound, as he squandered an early lead and was chased after 4 2/3 innings. Maholm allowed seven runs for the fourth time this season. Maholm has just not had the same consistency that he did a year ago, especially when it comes to keeping his sinking fastball down. It's been up too often, which is evident in Maholm's numbers. Maholm is 1-0 with a 2.31 ERA in five career starts against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Zito came through in his last start with one of his biggest wins as a Giant. He limited Atlanta to one run and three hits in seven innings last Thursday in a 5-1 triumph. That snapped a personal two-game losing streak for Zito, who endured a tough-luck loss to Pittsburgh on July 18 when he worked 6 1/3 innings in a 2-0 Pirates win. Zito is 71-37 with a 3.45 ERA in his career after the All-Star break. He's also 2-4 with a 4.45 ERA in nine starts at home this year.
away_pitcher_note: Staked to an early lead in his last start, Morton couldn't hold it. He fell behind hitters consistently and still showed a bit of struggle in harnessing what can be electric movement of his pitches. Morton admitted afterward to not feeling sharp from the get-go, and it was evident as he labored to locate through the 4 2/3-inning start. That start came on the heels of Morton throwing seven scoreless innings against the Giants. Now almost two months since being put in the rotation, Morton is still searching for that start-to-start consistency.

home_pitcher_note: Cain made his best run at the Cy Young Award in his last start with an impressive win over the Rockies. Cain threw 117 pitches in seven innings and yielded an earned run on three hits with five strikeouts. The victory vaulted the Giants into a tie with the Rockies at the time for the National League's Wild Card lead. Cain ended July with a 3-0 record and a 1.23 ERA. Cain's best month, career-wise has been in August where he's 9-6 with a 2.85 ERA. His next opponent is the Pirates and against them on July 19, Cain went seven and gave up an earned run on five hits with eight strikeouts for his 11th win.
away_pitcher_note: Duke wasn't at his sharpest in his last start, one in which he allowed 10 hits in six innings. However, as he's shown a knack for doing all season, he limited the damage -- this time to three runs. The consistency shown by Duke early in the season has taken a bit of a hit, but there's no reason to expect anything less than a six-inning start from the lefty each time out. He is just 1-5 on the road since the end of April and has a 2-2 record and 4.06 ERA in six career starts against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: For the second straight outing, Sanchez was unhittable for the most part. But when he did get hit, the damage was severe. Against the Rockies on Saturday, he surrendered five runs on five hits with four walks and five strikeouts in five-plus innings of work in a 8-2 loss. He gave up a three-run home run in the fourth to Troy Tulowitzki to break a scoreless tie. In the start before against the Braves, he gave up three runs on four hits in six innings. All three runs allowed came on two home runs. If he can keep the long ball at bay in his next start at home against the defending champion Phillies, it should serve him as well as in his no-hitter on July 10 against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez is going to force the Phillies to make a tough decision on him next month. He is 3-0 with a 3.09 ERA. He has thrown at least six innings in three of those starts, including Saturday against the Cardinals at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed three runs in six innings in the 14-6 victory. But as well as Lopez has pitched, the Phillies are grooming Pedro Martinez for a spot in the rotation. That would seem to put Lopez's job in jeopardy.

home_pitcher_note: The magic Sadowski had to begin his Major League career might officially be gone. After starting his career with 13 scoreless innings in his first two starts, Sadowski has surrendered 14 runs (13 earned) in his past 11 1/3 innings. In his last start, Sadowski was replaced after just 2 2/3 innings. He yielded three runs on five hits, walking three. For Sadowski to be successful, he needs to trust his stuff, attack the zone and find a way to miss bats. The first two items will help reduce his walk total, which is 14, while missing bats could lead to more strikeouts, of which he also has 14 on the season.
away_pitcher_note: Phillies fans eagerly await Cliff Lee's Phillies debut. The Phillies acquired him in a trade Wednesday with the Indians. The Phillies are hoping the 2008 American League Cy Young winner can provide a good 1-2 punch atop the rotation with Cole Hamels. Fans are hoping Lee is the missing ingredient to the Phillies repeating as World Series champions, and giving them another parade down Broad Street. "Hopefully I can help them repeat," Lee said. "That's the ultimate goal."

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum didn't allow an earned run -- he allowed two unearned -- in his complete-game effort Monday against the Pittsburgh Pirates. He allowed just four hits and struck out a career-high 15 batters. In fact, he's whiffed eight or more in nine straight outings. It's all keeping the right-hander on pace with teammate Matt Cain and the rest of the National League's elite pitchers. Lincecum went 1-0 with a 1.29 ERA in two starts against the Philadelphia Phillies last season.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton has been phenomenal over the past two months. He tied his season high by lasting eight innings against the Cardinals on Sunday, allowing two runs and striking out six. In July, he has surrendered just four runs in 29 1/3 innings, good for a 1.21 ERA. He is 5-1 since May 9. The lone loss? He allowed two runs and struck out 10 Rays on June 24. Against the Giants, Blanton is 1-2 with a 5.74 ERA in five career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Barry Zito finished one out shy of notching his third straight quality start Tuesday against the Pittsburgh Pirates. The veteran lefty allowed one earned run over 5 2/3 innings before giving way to the Giants 'pen. While his 4.54 ERA could come down a bit, Zito has also managed to get by while receiving zero runs of support in seven of his 21 starts this season. Zito didn't face the Phillies last season but holds a 2-1 record and 3.50 ERA against Philadelphia all-time.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels is 3-0 with a 2.45 ERA (nine earned runs in 33 innings) in his past five starts. The Phillies have won each of those games. Hamels has thrown at least seven innings in his previous two starts, the first time this season he has done that. "That's something I've really worked on, trying to go deep into the game," Hamels said. "Then you feel like you've really pitched and have actually helped the team. That's what I was able to do [Tuesday in Arizona]. I was able to throw strikes and battle all the way to the end."

home_pitcher_note: Four of Hampton's six wins this year have come against the Pirates. He was rocked for eight hits and a season-high nine runs in his previous start Wednesday in Chicago, losing to the Cubs for the first time since 2000. He's 15-4 with a 3.59 ERA in 26 career appearances (23 starts) against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Cain is certainly setting the pace for his fellow National League Cy Young Award candidates, teammate Tim Lincecum among them. Wednesday against the Pittsburgh Pirates, Cain allowed just three hits and whiffed four over nine innings of work but received a no-decision in the Giants' extra-inning victory. The right-hander has received 5.15 runs of support per game, the most among San Francisco's starters. He finished July with a 3-0 record and 1.23 ERA. In his lone start against the Houston Astros in 2008, Cain pitched eight innings and won.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino was called up from Triple-A Round Rock to take the spot of Roy Oswalt, who injured his back in his last start last Tuesday at Wrigley Field.
