home_pitcher_note: Even with the presence of his star-studded rotation mates, Sanchez is as good a choice as any to start San Francisco's home opener. He entrenched himself in franchise lore last July 10 by pitching the Giants' first no-hitter in 33 years, defeating San Diego, 8-0. Only an eighth-inning fielding error separated Sanchez from a perfect game that night. Sanchez finished the exhibition season with plenty of momentum. In his final three starts, he recorded a 0.55 ERA (one earned run) with eight hits allowed, five walks and 15 strikeouts in 16 1/3 innings. "I've got my confidence, and my stamina's there," said Sanchez, who's 1-2 with a 5.30 ERA in five career outings against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson made seven starts after returning from Tommy John surgery last year and enters this year with the belief that his arm is stronger than it has been at any point over the past eight years.  The former A's ace returns to the Bay Area to make his season debut with the hope of prolonging his recent success against the Giants. Since going 0-3 with a 7.50 ERA against them during a three-start stretch against that extended from 2003-06, he has opposed them three times and gone 2-0 with a 3.91 ERA. He is 1-2 with a 3.86 ERA in four career starts at AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: The 31-year-old will make his regular-season debut for the Giants, the fifth Major League team he has played for. A non-roster invitee to Spring Training, Wellemeyer beat out top prospect Madison Bumgarner and big Minor League winner Kevin Pucetas for the fifth starter's spot. Wellemeyer believes that he has regained the stuff he maintained in 2008, when he was 13-9 with a 3.71 ERA for St. Louis. He lost that sharpness, he said, by throwing too much in the 2008-09 offseason and slumped to 7-10 with a 5.89 ERA last year. Wellemeyer has started only one regular-season game at AT&T Park and owns no record in seven career appearances (including one start) against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: While allowing five earned runs in six innings against the Cubs on Opening Day, Lowe didn't get the results he was targeting after overhauling his delivery during the offseason and finding some success during Spring Training. All of the damage he incurred came courtesy of a pair of home runs. But the veteran sinkerballer was able to consistently keep his pitches down in the zone and consequently, he recorded nine groundball outs. He is 5-5 with a 3.10 ERA in 15 career starts against the Giants. But he has allowed just one run in his past 16 innings against them and 4-1 with a 2.13 ERA in his last nine starts against them.

home_pitcher_note: The Giants' ace looked every bit like the two-time reigning National League Cy Young Award winner that he is in Monday's season opener at Houston, surrendering four hits, walking none and striking out seven in seven shutout innings. Lincecum has thrived against Atlanta, posting a 5-1 mark with a 2.72 ERA in six career outings against the Braves. That included a memorable game at Turner Field in August 2008 when Lincecum, feeling discombobulated in the middle innings, began pitching from the stretch to regain his coordination and effectiveness. Somewhat surprisingly, Lincecum has been only slightly more successful at home (21-8, 2.84 ERA) than on the road (19-9, 2.97). His 90 lifetime appearances are evenly split between home and away.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami enters his second Major League season more comfortable with his surroundings and armed with a two-seam fastball that he began toying with after last year's All-Star break. The 34-year-old right-hander provided some optimism when he posted a 3.42 ERA in his final 21 starts last season. He allowed three earned runs in 5 2/3 innings when he faced the Giants in San Francisco in May and then limited them to one run in five innings during a July start against them in Atlanta. With the two-seamer, he is hoping to induce more ground balls and consequently pitch deeper into games. He pitched into the seventh inning in just six of his 25 starts last year.

home_pitcher_note: Barry Zito hopes to continue establishing a new trend when he faces the Pittsburgh Pirates. Known for his subpar first-half pitching, Zito blanked Houston for six innings in his season debut last Tuesday. Zito typically performs well against Pittsburgh with little to show for it, having posted an 0-3 record with a 3.13 ERA in four starts against the Pirates. This will be Zito's first start of the season at AT&T Park, where he finished 6-6 with a 3.92 ERA last year.
away_pitcher_note: Burres has been called up from Triple-A Indianapolis to make an emergency start for Ross Ohlendorf, who has been scratched due to back spasms. Burres had already been scheduled to make his first start of the season on Monday. Though this will be Burres' debut for the Pirates, he has made 41 Major League starts, including two last season with the Blue Jays. The left-hander is 13-19 with a 5.85 ERA in those previous big league starts. This will be Burres' first career start against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Cain sustained a strong 6 2/3-inning effort in his 2010 debut last Wednesday at Houston, but surrendered three of the four runs he allowed in his final inning. The Giants scored six runs in the final two innings to win, 10-4, though Cain emerged with no decision. Cain didn't issue a walk, which reflects his annual goal of improving his control. Cain excelled against Pittsburgh last year, posting a 1-0 record with a 0.56 ERA in two starts. Since this is Cain's first start at AT&T Park this season, it's worth noting that he compiled identical 7-4 records home and away a year ago. His ERA was slightly lower at home (2.72, compared to 3.09 on the road).
away_pitcher_note: Despite allowing four runs in six innings, Maholm left the mound after his first start of the season feeling good about the big picture. Things finally clicked with his curveball and changeup after the lefty struggled with both pitches all spring. Maholm's outing largely came down to two unexecuted pitches, and he was kicking himself afterward about the pitch selection of both. In each case, Maholm said, he chose to throw a pitch that his mind told him not to. Maholm is 1-1 with a 2.85 ERA in six career starts against San Francisco.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez received the distinction of pitching the Giants' home opener last Friday and had decent stuff, striking out six in 4 1/3 innings. But he wasn't consistent with his fastball, which prevented him from getting ahead on the count to most hitters. That, in turn, shortened his outing, though San Francisco proceeded to outlast Atlanta, 5-4, in 13 innings. Sanchez did not face the Pirates last season and is 0-1 with a 14.04 ERA in four lifetime appearances against them.
away_pitcher_note: Morton said he learned a valuable lesson while being hit hard in his first start of the season Friday in Arizona: Don't be afraid to rely on the fastball to get ahead of hitters and gain the advantage. Morton did that while striking out five in the first two innings, then absorbed a six-run third in which four of the D-backs' six hits came either on the first pitch or when ahead in the count. The 26-year-old righty has fared well in three career starts against the Giants, holding them to five earned runs in 19 innings (2.37 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Padilla gets a third chance to justify his selection as Opening Day starter. The first two tries didn't go very well, with an 11.42 ERA and 18 baserunners allowed in 8 2/3 innings. He's failed to get out of the fifth inning both times. Padilla showed his value after joining the Dodgers for last year's stretch run, but he's since been shot in the thigh and fought through forearm discomfort in Spring Training. He said neither problem bothers him, but he doesn't look like the same pitcher. His hard sinker is hanging and he's been very hittable. He's also hit two batters, a trouble sign considering his previous reputation as a headhunter. He was 1-0 in two starts against the Giants last year.
away_pitcher_note: The Giants obviously have confidence in Wellemeyer, since Thursday's scheduled off-day could have allowed them to skip his turn. Wellemeyer's Giants debut last Saturday began in promising fashion as he blanked Atlanta on four hits through five innings. But after he allowed a Jason Heyward homer in the sixth, the Braves nicked him for three runs in the seventh and proceeded to win. Wellemeyer has made six career appearances against Los Angeles with no decisions and a 4.26 ERA. That includes four outings, all but one in relief, and a 4.00 ERA at Dodger Stadium.
summary: 2010-04-16 - San Francisco Giants (8) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (10) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Yes, it's Charlie Haeger time again. He started Sunday, he relieved Wednesday and Haeger said he's good to go for his scheduled start Saturday against the Giants. The knuckleballer struck out 12 Marlins in six innings in his season debut, the most strikeouts to open a season by a Dodgers starter since Don Drysdale fanned 14 in 1960. Haeger has quickly earned the reliance of manager Joe Torre because of his resilience, but also because he's been effective. While the knuckler dances, he has enough of a fastball to keep hitters off-balance. And at a time when the Dodgers are getting a steady diet of short starts, he's capable of pitching deep into games.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum has worked seven innings in each of his two starts. His only lapse was Brian McCann's two-run, first-inning homer last Sunday for Atlanta. Lincecum has had mixed success at Dodger Stadium, where he's 1-1 with a 4.50 ERA in four outings. His most recent appearance in Chavez Ravine, last Sept. 20, was atypical. He allowed five runs and four hits in only four innings while walking four and striking out just three. Andre Ethier ranks among Lincecum's most significant Dodgers tormentors with a .294 average (5-for-17) and one home run off him.
summary: 2010-04-17 - San Francisco Giants (9) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw beat himself up after his last start, and he was the winning pitcher. He made it into the sixth inning, an improvement on his 4 2/3-inning  season debut, and he picked up his first win since last July, but he walked five and now has 11 walks in 10 innings. It's easy to forget that Kershaw is only 22, but the Dodgers are counting on him to take his game to the next level and not show the inconsistency that plagued him over the first half last year. He was able to work in off-speed pitches in his last start, but struggled with command of his fastball. As important as his other pitches are, Kershaw's calling card is an overpowering fastball that he needs to throw for strikes from the outset.
away_pitcher_note: Zito, who has made 100 starts as a Giant, is 2-0 for only the second time in his career. He hasn't started this well in any of his nine previous full seasons since 2003, when he pitched for Oakland. Zito proceeded to finish that season with a career-high 231 2/3 innings, as well as 14-12 record and a 3.30 ERA. That was one year after he won the American League Cy Young Award with a 23-5 mark and a 2.75 ERA. Zito is 6-5 with a 4.46 ERA in 13 career starts against Los Angeles, including 4-2, 3.62 in six Dodger Stadium assignments.
summary: 2010-04-18 - San Francisco Giants (1) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: For five innings in his last start against the Braves, Richard matched talented second-year pitcher Tommy Hanson. Richard cruised early, needing 63 pitches to get through the first five innings. He allowed three hits to that point and finished the fifth inning with back-to-back strikeouts, getting Melky Cabrera on a cutter down and in on the hands and then Hanson to end the inning, with Yunel Escobar stranded at third base. "Clayton threw the ball well," Black said. "I thought his stuff was crisp. I liked his tempo, the pace in between pitches and the way he attacks hitters." Richard ran out of gas in the sixth inning and allowed three runs, including a two-run double to Brian McCann.
away_pitcher_note: Cain has pitched more games against San Diego, 18, than any other club except Colorado (also 18). He's 4-6 against the Padres despite having posted a respectable 2.91 ERA. That includes a 1-4 mark at PETCO Park, where Cain's ERA is 2.87. Last year, Cain was 1-1 with a 2.84 ERA in three starts against the Padres. In his last outing, Cain yielded three runs and five hits in the first three innings to Pittsburgh before retiring the final 10 batters he faced.
summary: 2010-04-19 - San Francisco Giants (2) @ San Diego Padres (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Latos burned through 50 pitches in the first two innings of his last start against the Braves, the result of losing command of his fastball after a few close calls didn't go his way -- and raised his ire. Specifically, a 2-2 slider he threw to Martin Prado, the second hitter of the game, that missed, though not by much in his eyes. Prado, on the seventh pitch of an exhausting at-bat, hit the next pitch over the wall in left field for a home run. Two batters later, Latos walked Brian McCann on six pitches. All told, the 22-year-old allowed three runs in 4 2/3 innings with two walks and three strikeouts. This was only the 12th career Major League start for Latos, who made his Major League debut a year ago.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Sanchez posted perhaps the best outing by a Giants pitcher this year. Displaying the same kind of stuff he used to no-hit San Diego last July 10, Sanchez three-hit Pittsburgh through eight shutout innings. He struck out 11, matching the career high he established in his no-no. Lifetime, Sanchez is 2-2 with a 2.76 ERA against San Diego.
summary: 2010-04-20 - San Francisco Giants (0) @ San Diego Padres (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Garland, a free-agent acquisition in January, is winless after three starts for the Padres, though he pitched better in his last start on Friday against his former team, the Diamondbacks. Garland originally allowed three runs over five innings, though a scoring change the following day was kind to him. A third-inning hit (Conor Jackson) was changed to an error on third baseman Chase Headley, meaning Garland didn't allowed any earned runs in the game. Instead of having a 5.40 ERA, it is 3.60. He only got four ground-ball outs, which is far below where the sinkerballer would like to be.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer will attempt to improve upon his previous start, when he opened San Francisco's two-city trip by lasting only four innings and allowing seven runs at Los Angeles. Wellemeyer surrendered three homers in the first two innings, including a pair by Andre Ethier -- one a grand slam -- and a two-run clout by Matt Kemp. In three lifetime appearances against San Diego, Wellemeyer is 2-0 with a 4.73 ERA.
summary: 2010-04-21 - San Francisco Giants (2) @ San Diego Padres (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum is off to a 3-0 start for the first time in his career. Though his velocity has diminished slightly, he still has enough on his fastball to set up an improving slider, an effective curveball and his devastating changeup. Lincecum has started only once at home thus far, allowing Brian McCann's two-run homer and nothing else in seven innings while striking out 10 as the Giants defeated Atlanta, 6-3. Lincecum has thrived against St. Louis, winning each of his four starts while posting a 1.61 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lots of guys perform well in Spring Training, especially in the late innings against Minor Leaguers. They don't all carry it over, but Garcia assuredly has. He's turned in two excellent starts since winning the Cardinals' fifth starter job coming out of camp. He'll be going up against a stud opponent, but that hasn't fazed the rookie thus far. Garcia's two starts have found him opposing Yovani Gallardo and Johan Santana, so it shouldn't be an issue. Garcia has kept his poise despite limited experience, and there's little doubt about his stuff.
summary: 2010-04-23 - St. Louis Cardinals (1) @ San Francisco Giants (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The second-half Zito might have shown up early this year. Zito, who typically struggles before the All-Star break and excels afterward, has limited opponents to a .176 batting average. Zito has struck out just nine batters but has walked only five in 19 1/3 innings. He's coming off a no-decision last Sunday at Los Angeles, where he lasted 7 1/3 innings and left with a 1-0 lead after walking Garret Anderson. Manny Ramirez's pinch-hit homer off Sergio Romo then changed everything. Zito has struggled against St. Louis, going 0-4 with a 5.54 ERA in five lifetime starts.
away_pitcher_note: When his team needed him to help rest the bullpen, Wainwright delivered an outstanding game. But it's getting to the point where all he does is deliver outstanding games. Wainwright pitches deep into games, gets groundballs and strikeouts and even plays a complete game to boot. He's the reigning Gold Glover at his position and a viable candidate to win a Silver Slugger as well. He does it all, and there's no reason to think he'll stop this weekend at AT&T Park. Over his last 30 starts, dating back to mid-May of last season, Wainwright is 19-7 with a 2.17 ERA.
summary: 2010-04-24 - St. Louis Cardinals (0) @ San Francisco Giants (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Cain's lack of decisions obscures the fact that each of his outings has been a "quality" start. He owns an excellent strikeout-to-walk ratio of 4 to 1, reflecting his annual goal of cutting down on his walks. Cain issued 91 free passes in 217 2/3 innings in 2008, then walked 73 in the same number of innings last year. Cain picked up his first career victory against the Cardinals last year, yielding two runs (one earned) in 6 1/3 innings on May 29 at AT&T Park. He pitched even better but received no decision on July 1 at St. Louis, surrendering one run in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Penny keeps cruising. It looked like he might hit a bump in the road early in his last start, but instead he turned in another solid, seven-inning, two-run performance. He's throwing strikes, and more than that, he's throwing good strikes. He's working very efficiently, averaging almost exactly 14 pitches per inning. Since Penny was let go by the Red Sox and joined the Giants last summer, he's gone at least seven innings with two or fewer earned runs in eight of his nine starts. Penny also loves pitching at AT&T Park,  where he has a lifetime 3.05 ERA in 14 starts.
summary: 2010-04-25 - St. Louis Cardinals (2) @ San Francisco Giants (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The Giants believe Sanchez didn't get what he deserved the last time he was on the mound, and understandably so. He tossed a one-hitter in a 1-0 loss to San Diego. It was the Giants' first loss in 24 one-hit efforts since the franchise moved to San Francisco in 1958. He struck out 10 against the Padres, his second consecutive double-digit total. In the second inning, he walked the bases loaded, but struck out the side.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay is having his way four starts into his National League career. He already has thrown one shutout and one other complete game. He has walked just three batters. He has struck out 28. He is one of just three pitchers to start 4-0 with an ERA under 1.00 ERA in his first four starts with a team. Fernando Valenzuela (Dodgers in 1981) and Cliff Lee (Phillies in 2009) are the others.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer owns an 8.67 ERA, the result of three poor outings. His worst was April 16 against the Dodgers, when he allowed seven runs, six hits and three walks in four innings. He went 6 1/3 innings and allowed four runs, three hits and four walks in a loss to the Padres on April 21. He's been better against right-handed hitters, with a .182 average against, but left-handers are batting .385.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer took a step forward Thursday in Atlanta, where he allowed four hits and two unearned runs in six innings against the Braves. Phillies starters not named Roy Halladay have struggled this season, so Moyer could provide the Phillies a boost with consecutive solid performances. Moyer is 0-2 with a 7.36 ERA in two career appearances at AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: Even on a night when Lincecum didn't have his best control in the early going Friday against the Cardinals, the two-time Cy Young winner still struck out eight and allowed just one run in the 4-1 win that stopped a four-game losing streak. Even if he didn't have it all flowing, his grittiness in the outing impressed his fellow teammates and showed something in itself. With runners on first and second and none out, he got Albert Pujols to pop out and Matt Holliday to ground into a double play. Lincecum has at least seven strikeouts in each start this season and boasts a 1.00 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Just when it looks like Hamels is about to take a step forward, he takes a step backward. He allowed four home runs Friday against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field. If he encounters similar problems Wednesday against the Giants, it likely would not result in a good outcome for the Phillies. They are facing Giants ace Tim Lincecum.

home_pitcher_note: Zito is off to the best start of his career. Skeptics warned before his most recent outing that he wasn't amassing many strikeouts (nine in 19 1/3 innings), often an ominous sign for a pitcher. Then he struck out 10 in eight innings against St. Louis, marking his second double-digit strikeout performance as a Giant. Zito has been especially tough on the Rockies, compiling a 4-2 record with a 1.98 ERA against them in 11 lifetime starts, including 2-0 with a 0.95 ERA last year.
away_pitcher_note: Aaron Cook rebounded from a rough start to his season to notch his first win in style, going the distance in an 8-1 victory over the Marlins to secure a split in a Coors Field doubleheader.  Boasting what he called his best sinker in two years, Cook recorded 15 ground-ball outs while scattering five hits and two walks over nine innings. He had complete control of the strike zone, executing first-pitch strikes and first-pitch outs, efficiently working through 111 pitches and saving the bullpen on an early season twin bill. The "vintage Aaron Cook" outing earned him his all-time best 32nd win at Coors Field, surpassing Jason Jennings for the most wins in one of baseball's most challenging parks for pitchers.

home_pitcher_note: After opening the season with three consecutive quality starts, Cain lapsed slightly last Sunday against St. Louis, yielding two runs and six hits in five innings as the Giants lost, 2-0. There was no shame in Cain's game, considering that one of the runs he yielded was on an Albert Pujols homer. Cain, who made his Major League debut against Colorado on Aug. 29, 2005, has faced the Rockies 18 times, more than any other club except San Diego (19). He's 8-6 with a 3.31 ERA lifetime against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: As expected, Rogers was recalled from Triple-A to make the start on Saturday. He last pitched on Sunday in Reno for the Colorado Springs Sky Sox. He was stretched out to 75 pitches, finishing five innings and allowing five hits and one earned run. The good news is that he walked one. He pitched one-hit ball over five innings in his previous start against Las Vegas. He'll be making his second career start and his fifth Major League appearance.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez has put up some eye-popping statistics, including strikeouts per nine innings (12.22) and opponents' batting average (.167). Left-handed batters are 0-for-14 off him. Before his most recent outing, in which he worked five innings against Philadelphia, he recorded back-to-back double-digit strikeout games for the first time in his career -- April 14 against Pittsburgh and April 20 against San Diego. Sanchez is 2-3 with a 6.85 ERA in 15 career appearances against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Recalled on Tuesday, Chacin got the jitters out with a strong ninth inning in the Rockies' 12-1 victory over the D-backs at Coors Field. He struck out two and pitched around an error. Considered the Rockies' closest-to-the-Majors pitching prospect, Chacin has stellar secondary pitches. The question heading into the season was whether he could command the fastball at a Major League level. After going 3-0 with a 1.69 ERA in four starts at Triple-A Colorado Springs, Chacin gets his chance.

home_pitcher_note: Why Sanchez has made progress in his last two starts is pretty basic. The right-hander is throwing strikes more regularly. Even though he suffered a loss on April 27 to the Padres, Sanchez was effective over 6 1/3 innings, allowing three runs (two earned). Of his 101 pitches, 65 were strikes, as he struck out seven and walked two. In his previous outing -- April 22 at Houston -- Sanchez threw 89 pitches with 65 strikes in a win. He has walked two in his last 13 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Lincecum was three outs away from becoming the first Giants pitcher to win not only his first five starts of the season, but also five games in April, since John Burkett in 1993. A complete game also appeared within reach for Lincecum, who had surrendered three hits, struck out 11 and thrown 98 pitches entering the ninth. But after walking Shane Victorino on four pitches with one out, Giants manager Bruce Bochy pulled Lincecum in favor of closer Brian Wilson. Wilson blew the save, the Giants lost and Lincecum remained 4-0 with a 1.27 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After going on short rest in his previous start, Robertson will be well-rested for his sixth start of the season. Due to two scheduled team days off, the left-hander will be taking the mound exactly one week after his last outing. On April 28 against the Padres, Robertson was going on three days' rest. For four innings, it wasn't a factor, as he allowed just one hit in that span. But everything changed in the fifth. Robertson faced six batters in the inning, and all reached. He was charged with five runs, all in the inning. He threw 79 pitches and lost his second straight decision.
away_pitcher_note: Zito is 4-0 for the first time in his career. He was 0-7 over his last two Aprils. He's posted five consecutive quality starts. In his last one, he allowed two runs over eight innings. The four consecutive wins is his longest such streak since winning six straight from May 17, 2006, to June 16, 2006, with the Oakland A's.

home_pitcher_note: Mechanically and physically, Nolasco wasn't himself in his last start. The right-hander admitted it was one of those days where he didn't feel quite right. That happens over the course of a season. Nolasco worked four innings, giving up five runs while striking out seven in a loss to the Nationals. It was Nolasco's shortest stint since working 3 1/3 innings on Aug. 12, 2009 against Houston. Lifetime, he is 1-1 with a 1.13 ERA against San Francisco.
away_pitcher_note: Cain fanned eight and allowed only one hit and three walks in eight shutout innings against the Rockies. It was his first win, and it also lowered his ERA from 3.80 to 2.84. He hadn't struck out eight since Sept. 27 last year, and against Colorado they were mostly on his fastball, which was spot-on. It was the third time in his career he's allowed one hit and no earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: The perfect record and streak of scoreless innings are gone, obliterated by the Phillies' onslaught on Saturday in Philadelphia. Pelfrey now faces a challenge as great as Chase Utley, Ryan Howard, Jayson Werth and Shane Victorino -- getting back on the bike. Given the resolve he demonstrated through 27 innings of threats and zeroes, no one anticipates Pelfrey taking a giant step in the wrong direction because of a six-run one-inning blemish. When he opposes the Giants on Friday night, he will have had five days' rest, one more than normal, after a grueling 82-pitch start. He has pitched effectively in three career outings against the Giants, producing a 1-1 record and a 1.77 ERA. They have batted merely .187 in 20 1/3 innings against him. Pelfrey's ERA is 1.00 in three night starts and in three starts at Citi Field, where he's 3-0 this season. Left-handed hitters have a .292 slugging percentage in 48 at-bats against him this season. No Giants have more than six at-bats against Pelfrey.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez has struggled in his career against Colorado, and Sunday was no different. Sanchez, who came into the game 2-3 with a 6.85 ERA in 15 career appearances against the Rockies, allowed three runs in 4 2/3 innings to take the loss, raising his ERA to 2.48. Sanchez still has a strikeout-to-walk ratio of 37-28, but did walk five batters in each of his past two outings. In April, he recorded back-to-back double-digit strikeout games for the first time in his career -- April 14 against Pittsburgh and April 20 against San Diego. In four career starts against the Mets, the left-hander is 2-1 with 13 walks, 26 strikeouts and a 3.91 ERA. New York has a .234 batting average against him in that span. He has made one start at Citi Field, in which he allowed two runs and four hits in seven innings but did not get a decision.
summary: 2010-05-07 - San Francisco Giants (4) @ New York Mets (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The worst start of Johan Santana's career came last Sunday night at Citizens Bank Park, where he served up four home runs and 10 total runs against the Phillies. Citing a lack of fastball command, Santana walked 47-year-old pitcher Jamie Moyer with the bases loaded, then allowed a grand slam to Shane Victorino. He would prefer to forget all that on Saturday against the Giants, a team that has never beaten him in five career meetings. Last year, Santana went 1-0 with a 5.27 ERA in two starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer comes into this game against the Mets with an undesirable record and ERA. However, he has come on strong of late. Wellemeyer shined in his last start, which resulted in a 6-2 victory over Philadelphia on April 27. Wellemeyer went seven innings in the game, allowing two runs on three hits. Then, on Sunday against Colorado, he came in to relieve Jonathan Sanchez and pitched three scoreless innings. In four starts against New York, he has an 0-2 record, and the Mets have a .363 batting average against him. His ERA vs. New York is 6.67, and he has totaled 15 walks and 14 strikeouts. In one start at Citi Field, he is 0-1, having allowed five runs in 7 2/3 innings.
summary: 2010-05-08 - San Francisco Giants (4) @ New York Mets (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Neither Good Ollie nor Bad Ollie showed up on Monday in Cincinnati. Instead, some hybrid of the two walked four Reds batters but held them to two runs over six innings -- no small feat for a fly-ball pitcher at the Great American Ball Park. It was his second quality start in five tries this season. Perez has not faced his next opponent, the Giants, since June 2008, when he allowed five hits, two walks and six runs in 1/3 of an inning at AT&T Park. And the Giants are an improved offensive club since then.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum fanned 13 Marlins batters on Tuesday and finally got the run support he'd been asking for, but unfortunately he allowed a three-run homer to Hanley Ramirez in the sixth inning. Dan Uggla later hit another three-run homer off reliever Sergio Romo to ensure another no-decision for the two-time Cy Young Award winner. Lincecum's final line: seven innings, five hits, three runs, one walk and 13 strikeouts. Take away the one mistake to Ramirez and it's another typical dominant Lincecum outing. In three career starts against the Mets, Lincecum is 0-1 with a 5.68 ERA. This will be his first start at Citi Field.
summary: 2010-05-09 - San Francisco Giants (6) @ New York Mets (5) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: LeBlanc didn't factor in the decision in his last start against the Rockies, but kept the Padres close, extending his scoreless streak to 20 1/3 innings before allowing two runs in the fifth inning. It appeared that streak was going to end sooner when the left-hander loaded the bases in the fourth inning with one out, the result of two singles and a walk. But he got out of that jam. "For the most part, the fastball was down and the changeup was down," Padres manager Bud Black said. "In the middle of the game, the fastball and changeup were up in the zone. But, six innings, two runs -- you can't complain about that."
summary: 2010-05-11 - San Diego Padres (3) @ San Francisco Giants (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Cain had a no-hitter through 5 2/3 innings against the Marlins before Chris Coghlan's single up the middle with two outs in the sixth. After his no-hit bid was over, Cain didn't let up. He finished with four hits allowed and two runs in seven-plus innings to earn his second win of 2010. Cain located his fastball well and worked in his breaking ball to keep the Marlins off-balance. Cane (2-1) is coming off two stellar starts. He allowed one hit in eight shutout innings against Colorado on May 1.
away_pitcher_note: Richard struggled during a five-inning stint in his last start against the Rockies where he allowed five runs and five walks. Richard allowed 10 baserunners and three runs in the first three innings, although the left-hander managed to exact a little revenge on the Rockies in the fourth when he helped his own cause with a two-run double to left field. "It was a game that doesn't go how you planned," Richard said. "Some of the pitches didn't go where I wanted them to. "It was not having command of my fastball. And when I don't have that, it's going to be a rough slide."
summary: 2010-05-12 - San Diego Padres (5) @ San Francisco Giants (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez is coming off a seven-inning outing at New York last Friday in which he matched a career high by throwing 115 pitches. So the extra rest from Monday's scheduled off-day could help him. Entering that game, Sanchez had not allowed a home run all season. But he allowed a career-high three that night, two to Ike Davis and one to Rod Barajas. Sanchez's stuff has remained decent all year, as demonstrated by his average of 10 strikeouts per nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Astros, Latos allowed two hits over eight scoreless innings, striking out nine with no walks as the Padres rolled to a 7-0 victory. Latos finished three outs shy of what would have been his first career shutout. But the Padres are watching the innings count of the 22-year-old and decided to be cautious. Latos, he of 16 career starts, mixed and matched his mid-90s fastball with a slider that was biting and a changeup that gave the Astros fits. Latos induced 10 ground outs, and, before striking out the final four hitters he faced, mostly got quick outs. The eight innings and the nine strikeouts were both career bests.
summary: 2010-05-13 - San Diego Padres (1) @ San Francisco Giants (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer received a no-decision in his most recent outing last Saturday at New York. He yielded three runs in the first two innings and ultimately settled down, though he lasted just 4 1/3 innings, allowing three runs and four hits. Wellemeyer also issued five walks and leads the team with 20 in 28 2/3 innings, which offsets his competent .229 opponents' batting average.
away_pitcher_note: The big right-hander is coming off his best start of the season Saturday against the Padres in Houston. He pitched seven innings and allowed five hits and two runs (one earned) and struck out 11 batters while not issuing any walks. Alas, he suffered the loss because the Astros scored one run. Paulino has lost each of his past five starts after getting a no-decision in his first start. Paulino's only previous career appearance at San Francisco was forgettable. He lasted only two innings and gave up nine hits and nine runs (eight earned) in a loss last July.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum pitched like the two-time Cy Young Award winner that he is against Houston in the season opener, allowing four hits while walking none and striking out seven in seven shutout innings. Lincecum is 7-for-7 in quality starts, limiting opponents to a .193 batting average overall and recording a 2.01 ERA at home -- which actually exceeds his 1.73 ERA on the road. Lincecum has sharpened his control, issuing an average of 1.9 walks per nine innings -- down from last year's figure of 2.7. He's also averaging 11.9 strikeouts per nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt has delivered a quality start in all seven of his outings this year but only has two wins to show for it. He's coming off a solid start against the Padres on Sunday in which he struck out nine batters and gave up six hits and three runs in eight innings. He got a no-decision. He pitched against the Giants and Tim Lincecum on Opening Day and took the loss after allowing seven hits and three earned runs in six innings. He's 5-6 with a 3.76 ERA in 25 starts against the Giants in his career, including a masterful effort last July in which he allowed three hits and one run in eight innings. He's 3-5 with a 4.39 ERA in nine career starts at AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: Zito is coming off his first loss of the season, a 3-2 setback against the San Diego Padres in which he surrendered three runs in five innings and equaled a career high by walking seven. Zito set the tone for his season by sparkling in his 2010 debut at Houston, allowing three hits while walking one and striking out five in six shutout innings. Zito has been equally effective against left- and right-handed batters, limiting the former group to a .200 average and the latter to a .197 figure.
away_pitcher_note: Myers is coming off a win at St. Louis in which he held the Cardinals to eight hits and two runs in six innings. He's thrown six innings or more in each of his seven starts, marking the second time he has done that. In 2003, he went six innings or more in his first 11 starts with the Phillies. He got a no-decision when he faced the Giants in the second game of the season April 14 in Houston, giving up 12 hits and four runs in six innings. He's 1-3 with a 6.75 ERA in eight career games (six starts) vs. the Giants, and 1-1 with a 4.85 ERA in four career games (two starts) at AT&T Park. Myers lost his first three starts against the Giants before beating them in 2006. He pitched against them twice in relief in 2007 and made one start against them in 2008 and didn't get a decision.

home_pitcher_note: Richard held the Giants to two runs over seven innings and one of those runs came when he was called for a balk with a runner on third in the second inning. "I felt good, and got ahead for the most part," said Richard, who allowed seven singles in his seven innings with two walks and two strikeouts. Richard worked 1-2-3 innings in the first and third innings but was stressed in the second, when he allowed four hits and two runs -- the last coming on a balk call by home-plate umpire Gary Darling. "From my perspective, I see a guy with a very good move," Black said. Richard even knocked in a run with a sacrifice fly.
away_pitcher_note: Cain has pitched effectively against the Padres in his career, but he doesn't have much to show for it. In his first 20 career starts against them, he's 4-7 with an ERA of 3.12. He lost to the Padres at home last Wednesday, allowing five runs on six hits in 6 2/3 innings. That's more runs than Cain allowed in his three previous starts, a span of 20 innings. It was also the most he's allowed this season. He gave up two runs on seven hits in six innings in his last start in San Diego but received a no-decision. The Giants have yet to beat the Padres in six games this season, a major reason why San Diego currently rules the NL West.
summary: 2010-05-17 - San Francisco Giants (1) @ San Diego Padres (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Latos, in his 17th Major League start, got his first shutout and, better still, carried a perfect game into the sixth inning before settling for a one-hitter, as the Padres completed a sweep of the Giants with a 1-0 victory at AT&T Park last week. "I just go out there and do my best. That's all I can do," said the soft-spoken Latos after the game. "Everything came together today." Latos needed 106 pitches to dispense with the Giants on a sun-splashed day where the spotlight focused on the powerful right arm -- and, for a time, the bat -- of the second-year pitcher who, the Padres believe, is just beginning to touch greatness. "He's maturing mentally and physically and he's learning how to make pitches when he needs to," Padres pitching coach Darren Balsley said.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez has allowed one or fewer runs in four of his first seven starts, giving up a combined 10 hits, and is 2-2 in those games. He's lost to the Padres twice this year already, each time by a 1-0 score. He's given up two runs on four hits in 15 innings against them. He does have two career wins over San Diego, including last year's no-hitter, and an ERA of 2.37 in 15 appearances against them. The left-hander has been a different pitcher this season. He's throwing with a lot more confidence and trusts his stuff more. He had 18 walks through his first five starts and has since settled down, walking one in each of his last two starts.
summary: 2010-05-18 - San Francisco Giants (7) @ San Diego Padres (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy has been Arizona's best pitcher this year. In his last start, against the Braves, Kennedy did not receive a decision because another meltdown by the bullpen cost him. The right-hander tossed six shutout innings before Brian McCann led off the seventh with a home run. After allowing back-to-back singles later in the inning, he was removed with a 4-1 lead, only to watch Juan Gutierrez give up a three-run homer to tie the game. Kennedy appeared in just one game for the Yankees in 2009 and four in Triple-A after missing most of the year following surgery to remove an aneurysm near his right shoulder. The right-hander came in the same three-team trade that netted the D-backs Edwin Jackson.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer is the Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde of the Giants pitching staff. At home, he's cool, calm and collected with a 2-1 mark and a 3.04 ERA. On the road, it's a completely different story. Away from the friendly confines of AT&T Park, it's a cruel world for the right-hander, who's 0-2 with a 9.49 ERA on the road. He's 1-3 with a 4.79 ERA against the Arizona Diamondbacks for his career, and he pitched fairly well in his only start at Chase Field. He wouldn't mind facing Adam LaRoche, though, as the first baseman is a lifetime .192 hitter (5-for-26) against him. Keep Stephen Drew away from Wellemeyer, however. Drew has six hits in nine at bats against Wellemeyer.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez was magnificent in his last start against the Braves. The right-hander allowed just one run over eight innings in an 11-1 win. Lopez could have gone out for the ninth, but the club elected to give the bullpen some work with such a big lead. Lopez has pitched at least seven innings in his past three starts and has been one of the club's most reliable starters. While not overpowering, Lopez has a good feel for pitching and manages a game well. He came to Spring Training as a non-roster invitee and pitched his way into the No. 4 spot in the rotation, besting Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey. The right-hander has battled arm troubles since being the ace of the Orioles' staff years ago. He throws a fastball, cutter, curveball, slider and changeup. Lopez appeared in seven games (five starts) for the Phillies last year and also started 18 games for Triple-A Lehigh Valley.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum has thrived against Arizona, as is the case with most opponents. He has averaged more than seven innings per start against the D-backs while compiling a 5-1 record with a 1.87 ERA in nine appearances. He has allowed the D-backs only 48 hits in 67 1/3 innings. Lincecum will be pitching on his usual four days' rest instead of the five he received before his last outing, a 2-1 triumph over Houston on Saturday. Lincecum worked eight innings but said afterward that he didn't feel as sharp as usual, so the extra rest might actually have hampered instead of helped him.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill turned in his longest outing of the year on Sunday, but was still the losing pitcher in a 4-0 defeat at Anaheim. He gave up three earned runs on five hits while striking out two and retired 13 straight batters at one point. Cahill faced the Giants once last year, giving up an earned run on four hits and a walk over seven innings. For his career, Cahill has fared much better during his 19 home appearances (8-9, 4.12 ERA) compared his 17 road starts (3-8, 5.20 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: This game could be regarded as a test for the new, improved Zito. Since joining the Giants, he's 0-3 with a 9.22 ERA in three starts against the A's, for whom he played from 2000-06. If Zito stays true to his 2010 form, he won't get caught up in facing his former team and will treat this game as he would any other. Naturally, Zito has pitched more at the Oakland Coliseum than anywhere else, compiling a 51-31 record with a 3.73 ERA in 111 starts there.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez threw his fifth quality start in eight tries on Monday, in an 8-4 A's win. He completed seven innings, giving up three earned runs on four hits and four walks while striking out four. Gonzalez said he's learned to control his emotions on the mound and that it's allowed him to pitch deeper in games this season. Gonzalez made one start against the Giants last year and was knocked around a bit. He lasted just 3 2/3 innings, giving up six runs (four earned) on 10 hits and two walks while striking out six.
away_pitcher_note: Cain's 2-4 lifetime record against the A's obscures the fact that he pitched his best career game against them: a one-hit shutout at Oakland on May 21, 2006. He has recorded six quality starts this season in eight outings, including last Monday, when he surrendered two runs in six innings but absorbed the decision in a 3-1 Giants loss at San Diego. Typically, all Cain needs is a little offense to succeed. He's 45-18 when he receives two or more runs of support and is 40-8 when he gets three runs or more while he's in the game.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets turned in his third straight quality outing on Tuesday in an extra-innings win over Seattle. He tossed 6 2/3 innings, his longest start of the year, giving up four earned runs on eight hits and four walks while striking out five. Sheets also set a new season high in pitches thrown (111). After Tuesday's contest, Sheets said he needs to focus on cutting down his walks, but that he's happy he was able to pitch deep into the game.
away_pitcher_note: Though Sanchez has allowed a season-high four runs in two of his last three starts, his control has improved in that span. He has walked just two batters in 21 innings in those games, including none in six innings in his most recent outing last Tuesday at San Diego. He's 8-7 with a 3.32 ERA and 161 strikeouts in 143 2/3 innings since his no-hitter last July 10 against the Padres. Sanchez already has pitched seven innings or more four times this season, matching the number he reached last year. Due to poor run support, he's only 1-2 in those games this year.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer was pounded in his last outing, a 13-1 loss at Arizona in which he yielded five runs in five innings. Three of the four hits he surrendered were home runs. But he sparkled one start earlier, limiting Houston to two runs and five hits in 7 1/3 innings in an 8-2 win on May 14 in San Francisco. Statistics reflect Wellemeyer's preference for pitching at home, where he's 2-1 with a 3.04 ERA compared with 0-3, 9.35 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: In Hernandez's last start, pitching on only three days' rest, he picked up a no-decision after allowing two runs on four hits in 6 1/3 innings against the Mets. Angel Pagan's inside-the-park home run in the fourth inning put the Mets up 1-0 early, but the Nationals rallied for a 5-3 victory. Hernandez is 4-6 against the Giants in his career with a 3.95 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum had by far his worst performance of the season last Thursday at Arizona, allowing five runs and five hits while walking five in five innings. He did strike out six, hiking his National League-leading total to 75. Something to consider when evaluating Lincecum's victory total: San Francisco's bullpen has blown four leads they have inherited from him. Lincecum has recorded a 1-0 record with a 1.77 ERA in three career appearances against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: After beginning his professional career with a strong 3-0 start -- including a six inning, one run debut against the Dodgers -- Atilano struggled in his most recent outing against the Mets. He gave up seven runs on nine hits over 4 1/3 innings pitched in a 10-7 loss. David Wright put the Mets ahead early on his three-run double to right-center field. New York added five more runs in the fifth inning. One inning later, Rod Barajas crushed a two-run home run to left-center field. Atilano has never faced the Giants in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Zito, who's 2-2 with a 4.33 ERA in six career appearances against Washington, allowed a season-high six runs and nine hits in 6 2/3 innings last Friday in a 6-1 Giants loss at Oakland. Two of those hits, however, were back-to-back bloop doubles that fueled a three-run third inning and skewed Zito's numbers. Zito's success this year is partly due to avoiding the long ball. He has allowed one home run in 61 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In Stammen's last outing, he got a no-decision after allowing four earned runs on nine hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Orioles.  He surrendered two home runs -- one an inside-the-park home run by Adam Jones in the fourth inning -- but the Nationals rallied to win, 7-6. Stammen has faced the Giants once in his career, taking a no-decision after giving up four earned runs on seven hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cain once again fell victim to the Giants' struggling bats in his last start against Oakland, when he was saddled with the loss despite allowing only one run on five hits in eight solid innings. It was the third straight losing decision for Cain, who regained his command (one walk) after walking 17 batters in his previous four starts combined (27 2/3 innings). Cain is 4-4 with a 3.86 ERA in 14 career starts against the D-backs. In his last start against Arizona on Sept. 22, 2009, Cain was chased after 2 1/3 innings after giving up seven runs on eight hits.
away_pitcher_note: Saturday evening at Chase Field, Jackson again failed to post back-to-back quality starts. Opposing the Toronto Blue Jays, the D-backs' No. 2 starter yielded five runs on six hits over 7 2/3 frames. A three-run, eighth-inning home run marred an otherwise solid outing. Jackson did strike out nine Jays batters and has whiffed at least seven in each of his last four starts. He has yet to really establish himself as a force in Arizona's rotation, however. Perhaps gearing up for a National League West rival will spur him toward greater success: Against the San Francisco Giants all-time, Jackson is 1-0 with a 3.38 ERA in two games.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing against Oakland, Sanchez held the A's to only two runs on three hits. But for the third time this season, Sanchez suffered a loss despite holding opposing bats to no more than three hits or two runs as he and the Giants lost, 3-0. Sanchez cruised until the seventh inning, when he gave up an RBI double to Oakland's Jake Fox and was removed in the eighth after leading off the inning with a walk. Sanchez has lost to Arizona more than any other team throughout his career, six times in 15 career appearances (12 starts). However, Sanchez made two of his final three starts of 2009 against Arizona, winning both while pitching into the sixth inning each time.
away_pitcher_note: Before Sunday's series finale with the Blue Jays, D-backs manager A.J. Hinch said he planned for Buckner to start against the San Francisco Giants. Then, against the Jays, Buckner allowed eight runs (seven earned) on 11 hits; he didn't record an out in Toronto's five-run fifth inning. The 26-year-old right-hander said afterward that he missed his desired location on a few of his pitches, but that the Jays also hit some of his so-called pitcher's pitches. Buckner, who has enlisted the advice of teammate Dan Haren regarding "minimizing the damage," is a safe bet to pitch in San Francisco. In four career appearances (two starts) opposing the Giants, Buckner is 0-1 with a 7.62 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After a 24 scoreless-inning slump by the Giants offense, Wellemeyer received the gift of run support in his last outing. Against Washington on Tuesday, Wellemeyer faced little trouble until the seventh, when he was pulled after giving up three straight singles to open the inning. The Giants bullpen allowed in one run on a sacrifice fly, but that was it as Wellemeyer finished with a final line of two runs on four hits and two strikeouts. Wellemeyer's last start against the D-backs was forgettable, as he gave up five runs on four hits -- three of which were home runs -- in a 13-1 pounding. Wellemeyer holds a 1-4 record and 5.61 ERA in eight career appearances (four starts) against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy has been the club's most consistent pitcher this year. In his last outing against the Rockies at Coors Field, Kennedy searched for a pitch that would work for him, but never could find it. Still, he managed to keep his team in the game, allowing just three runs in five innings of work. Two of the runs came via homers from Brad Hawpe and Troy Tulowitzki. Kennedy did not get much offensive support as the D-backs fell, 3-2. He appeared in just one game for the Yankees in 2009 and four in Triple-A after missing most of the year following surgery to remove an aneurysm near his right shoulder. The right-hander came in the same three-team trade that netted the D-backs Edwin Jackson.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum has allowed 11 runs in his last 9 2/3 innings after giving up 11 in his first 56 innings. He's losing command of the strike zone too, walking five in each of his past three starts. A blister problem that crept up during Spring Training may be affecting him more than he's willing to let on. The Washington Nationals took advantage of his wildness in scoring three runs on one hit in one inning during his last start. Two walks, a hit batter and three stolen bases in the fifth resulted in Lincecum's worst start since Sept. 23, 2008, against the Rockies, when he allowed six runs on six hits and five walks over 4 1/3 innings. He's 5-3 in 11 starts with a 3.52 ERA against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez improved upon his big league-leading numbers with his ninth win of the season on Wednesday night as he lowered his ERA to 0.88. He beat the D-backs for the second time this year and has not allowed a run in 17 innings. He'll be facing the Giants for the first time Monday, the only remaining team in the National League West yet to face Jimenez this season.

home_pitcher_note: Zito earned a no-decision in his last outing against Washington, allowing four runs (three earned) on seven hits in 6 1/3 innings. He also walked five. The lefty got off to a rocky start -- giving up a solo home run in the first and second innings -- but settled down until leaving with the bases loaded in the seventh. Zito is 5-2 with a 2.00 ERA in 12 career starts against the Rockies. Zito beat Colorado earlier this season on April 20, allowing two runs on five hits while striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel put together his best outing of the season against the D-backs on Thursday in an 8-2 win at Coors Field to help the Rockies clinch their first series sweep of the season. He matched a career high of eight strikeouts and also allowed fewer than three runs for the first time this season.

home_pitcher_note: A pitcher who has struggled to get run support throughout his career, Cain has proven he only needs a few runs to get the job done. He got one in the top of first inning in his last start and promptly went to work, throwing a one-hit shutout in a 4-0 win over Arizona. Cain also struck out a season-high nine batters, walking zero. In his last start against Colorado on May 1, Cain dazzled, tossing eight innings of one-hit ball and striking out eight to earn his first victory of the season. The right-hander is 9-6 with a 3.09 ERA in 19 career starts against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Francis was solid through five innings Friday against the Dodgers before allowing four runs in the sixth and taking the loss in his third start since returning from season-ending surgery in 2009. In eight career starts at AT&T Park, the lefty is 3-4 with a 5.86 ERA and one shutout.

home_pitcher_note: Duke has lost five of his past six decisions after winning his first two, with the Pirates giving him little run support. He allowed just one earned run in his previous two starts, getting a win and a no-decision, before allowing 12 hits and seven runs over 5 1/3 innings in a loss Friday in Atlanta. Although Duke is 1-2 at home, he has a 3.57 ERA in his six starts at PNC Park this year, and he is the all-time wins leader there with a 27-26 record. Duke will be facing the Cubs for the first time this season. He has allowed 85 hits in 63 2/3 innings, including seven homers, while striking out 40 and walking 23.
away_pitcher_note: A high pitch count limited Sanchez to only five innings in his last outing against Arizona, but the left-hander still was effective. Sanchez allowed just two hits -- one a solo home run -- and struck out seven. After struggling against Pittsburgh the first four times of his career, Sanchez turned in a gem of an outing against the Pirates his last time out. On April 14, Sanchez tossed eight innings of shutout ball, holding the Bucs to three hits while striking out a career-high 11.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm was effective on Sunday in Atlanta, limiting the Braves to just two earned runs on 10 hits while striking out five and walking three. He left after six, trailing 2-0 before the Pirates' comeback went for naught in a 5-2 loss. Maholm's first start of the year came in San Francisco, when he gave up three earned runs on eight hits over five innings while walking three and striking out three. He took a no-decision in the 6-5 Pittsburgh win. In seven career starts against the Giants, Maholm is 1-1 with a 3.13 ERA, giving up 16 earned runs and 44 hits over 46 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer pitched well in his past two starts, earning the win on Tuesday against Washington and giving up only two runs in his last outing against the D-backs, a no-decision. Of course, Wellemeyer's success in those outings should come as no surprise. Both came at AT&T Park, where the right-hander has shined this season. If history is any case, however, the stars certainly do not appear to align with him for his next outing. Wellemeyer is going on the road -- where he is 0-3 with a 9.35 ERA this season -- to PNC Park, where he is 0-2 with a 6.95 ERA in eight career outings (four starts).

home_pitcher_note: Relying more on his changeup against a struggling Cubs lineup on Memorial Day, Ohlendorf pitched his best game of the season, going for season highs of 103 pitches and 67 strikes over seven innings of one-run, three-hit ball. Ohlendorf also stuck out a season-high six batters while walking a season-low two. A defensive gaffe in the outfield eventually resulted in Chicago's lone run and ruined Ohlendorf's shot at his first win of the season in the 2-1 Pirates win. The outing marked his second consecutive quality start, though the first went for naught with the Pittsburgh bats lifeless in a 4-0 loss at Cincinnati May 26. The right-hander now appears fully recovered from the back spasms that kept him out for more than a month after his first start of the season, April 7. Ohlendorf's seventh start of the season will mark the first time in his young career that he has faced the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: The uncharacteristic struggles of Lincecum continued in his last start, a highly anticipated duel between Colorado's Ubaldo Jimenez, as the right-hander was saddled with his second consecutive loss. Lincecum failed to make it out of the sixth inning for the third straight outing, throwing 121 pitches (73 strikes) in 5 2/3 innings. He allowed four runs (thee earned) on six hits, and also walked five batters (two intentionally) for the fourth consecutive game. Lincecum has faced Pittsburgh three times in his career, posting a 1-1 record with 2.86 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto's four-game winning streak hit a speed bump on Tuesday in St. Louis, although he didn't take a loss despite allowing eight runs and 10 hits in just five innings. With the no-decision, Cueto still hasn't lost since April 24. In the starts between that loss and the eight-run outing in St. Louis, Cueto gave up a total of eight runs in six starts. Now, he'll try to bounce back from his roughest outing of the season against a team he's never faced. Cueto will pitch against the Giants for the first time in 72 career starts, and the only Giants batter who has faced him is former Pirate Freddy Sanchez.
away_pitcher_note: Zito entered his last start against Colorado having dominated the Rockies throughout his career, and his most recent outing was no different. Zito threw seven innings of one-run baseball, allowing four hits and striking out eight, earning a no-decision. The left-hander, already off to the best start of his career, lowered his ERA from 2.94 to 2.78. Next up for Zito is Cincinnati, whom he has had mixed results (3-2, 7.13 ERA) against in the past. He last faced the Reds on Aug. 19, 2009, allowing two hits in six shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: LeCure has started two games in place of the injured Homer Bailey and could be making his final start Tuesday before Bailey returns to the rotation. The right-hander allowed just two runs in six innings in a 15-6 win over Houston in his first start and gave up three runs in 5 1/3 innings in a 4-1 loss at St. Louis on Wednesday. Although LeCure has spent all year as a starter -- he went 5-2 with a 2.55 ERA in nine starts at Triple-A Louisville -- it's possible he could stay with the Reds as a reliever when Bailey returns.
away_pitcher_note: Cain earned his second straight win and evened his record at 4-4 in his last outing, a one-run, eight-inning gem against Colorado. Cain allowed four hits and struck out five, passing Jack Sanford for ninth on the all-time San Francisco Giants' strikeout list (Cain has 785). Cain is 2-3 with a 3.96 ERA in six career starts against the Reds. The right-hander faced Cincinnati twice in a two-week stretch last season. On August 3, he took the loss, allowing five runs in seven innings. He bounced back on Aug. 20, holding the Reds to one run in eight innings, eventually taking a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Harang gave up two runs on eight hits in his last start on Friday in Washington and lasted just four innings on a very warm night.
